posts.raw_content:
I suspect that China helped Lula steal the election. Brazil's voting machines are relatively protected from outside meddling, but highly susceptible to [insider attacks](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378214436_A_decade_probing_the_Brazilian_voting_machine)  China couldn't allow the US to seal off the Americas and they weren't about to lose control of a critical source of oil, iron and agricultural products.

The big question is, what are we going to do about it? Brazil is much bigger than Venezuela, but there's much more support for the right there. Are we going to let Lula become Chavez 2.0? 

Brazil's three main exports are Oil, Soybeans and Iron. China is their major trade partner $100B. This insulates Brazil from American embargo pressure, but more importantly, the Chinese are highly dependent on Brazil to feed their economy and their people.

Brazil has relatively small oil reserves (16B barrels) compared to Venezuela (303B barrels). However, it has a much more functional economy and exports much more ($44B) vs Venezuela ($5B). Most importantly, 50% of Brazil's oil exports go to China and that represents 14-18% of China's total imports.

Brazil exports $45B of soybeans. 71-74% goes to China.  That represents 60-73% of China's soybean imports. Most goes into animal feed. All told, Brazil is the source of 25-34% of China's agricultural imports. This includes 46% of their beef, 19% of their pork, 11% of their chicken and 29% of their sugar. All told, Brazil supplies China with 8-11% of their food supply.

Brazil exports $33B in iron of which 66% goes to China. That represents 22% of China's iron supply. The other major source is Australia, which is obviously an American ally.
